title: Mobile-Optimized AI-Driven Personalized Learning: A Case Study at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University
venue: International Journal of Interactive Mobile Technologies (iJIM)
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an AI-driven personalized learning platform, Campus+, improves undergraduate students’ academic achievement, engagement, motivation, and retention of course material. The authors frame the problem as a need to move beyond conventional uniform teaching toward personalized, adaptive support that can better fit learners’ needs, especially in a mobile-learning context.

The intervention is a mobile-optimized platform built with LangChain, Pinecone, and an LLM model. It lets instructors upload course materials and allows students to interact with an AI tutor through a chat interface embedded in their course documents. The system uses document retrieval and semantic search to provide personalized, real-time feedback and support, with the paper noting that it is based on GPT-4 and is positioned as an alternative to fine-tuning. The platform was used for four weeks by an experimental group, while a control group continued without the AI intervention.

The study was conducted at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University in Morocco with undergraduate students enrolled in thermodynamics, operational research, neuroanatomy, and embryology. Quantitative pre-test/post-test comparisons and survey feedback were used to evaluate the platform. The authors report that students using Campus+ showed greater gains than the control group, and that most users perceived it as effective for learning efficiency, engagement, motivation, and retention. The paper also notes risks and constraints, including possible bias in personalization and limited support for graphics, numbers, and mathematical formulas.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model used as the conversational AI engine for question answering and personalized support in a retrieval-augmented learning platform.
identified_tools.use_case: Used within Campus+ / Tutor GPT to answer student questions from uploaded course documents and provide personalized guidance and instant feedback; the system is described as using OpenAI GPT-4, LangChain, and Pinecone for document-based Q&A.

findings.finding_summary: The paper reports improved post-test performance for the experimental group using Campus+ compared with the control group across four subjects. In thermodynamics, the experimental group increased from 14.3375 to 15.0375 (mean diff. 0.7, t=5.83, p<0.001, df=7), while the control group increased only from 14.4 to 14.575.

In operational research, the experimental group increased from 14.12 to 14.74 (mean diff. 0.62, t=5.49, p<0.001, df=9), compared with a smaller increase in the control group from 14.68 to 14.81. The authors interpret this as evidence that the AI intervention improved learning outcomes.

In neuroanatomy, the experimental group rose from 14.27 to 14.93 (mean diff. 0.665, t=6.02, p<0.001, df=10), whereas the control group increased from 14.66 to 14.84. The paper states that the experimental group consistently improved more than the control group.

In embryology, the experimental group increased from 15.67 to 16.22 (mean diff. 0.55, t=5.24, p<0.001, df=8), compared with the control group’s increase from 14.74 to 14.91. The paper reports a stronger improvement for the AI-supported group.

Survey results suggest favorable learner perceptions of the system: 84% rated Campus+ as moderately or highly effective for improving learning efficiency, 80% reported feeling slightly or highly engaged, 73% said it increased their enthusiasm to learn, 80% reported moderate or excellent retention, and 88% rated the experience as slightly better or far superior to traditional methods.
findings.measure: Student self-report survey on effectiveness, engagement, motivation, retention, and comparison with traditional learning

quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental primary study with a control group and pre/post measures, plus survey data. It provides direct empirical evidence, but it is not a randomized trial and the paper does not report effect sizes or confidence intervals.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are moderate in magnitude in raw score change and consistently favor the AI-supported group across subjects, but the study does not provide standardized effect sizes. The evidence suggests meaningful positive impact, though the overall strength is limited by design and reporting constraints.
